LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Imitative Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative Speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how to take care of household items. 1. Why do we need various items in our homes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify positions of household items in relation to others
2. appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative Speaking helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify positions of household items in relation to others

What this means
In this part you learn to identify positions of household items in relation to others. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify positions of household items in relation to others.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify positions of household items in relation to others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative Speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative Speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify positions of household items in relation to others)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative Speaking to a partner. (skill: appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative Speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify positions of household items in relation to others.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative Speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative Speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Imitative Speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how to take care of household items. 1. Why do we need various items in our homes?
2. How can we tell the position of an item in the house?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative Speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify positions of household items in relation to others.
5. Be able to: appreciate use of prepositions in describing positions of objects.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
